findings.title: Removing files can compare shard payloads on the caller’s stack
findings.reproduction: A strict set retains two copies of the same shard. Calling without with both copies retained invokes duplicate resolution.
findings.expected: Operations comparing secret shard bytes run only on an admitted stack.
findings.observed: The strict wrapper calls the ordinary method directly. Duplicate resolution compares the surviving payload slices on that thread.
findings.impact: The operation can process payload bytes without satisfying the strict stack conditions. Mapping protection on the original buffers does not cover those temporaries.
findings.recommendedFix: Move the recomputation into strict(...) or restructure it to use verified public metadata only.
findings.requiredVerification: Cover retained duplicates with and without a protected stack; require refusal before comparison if a stack cannot be admitted.

findings.title: Lazy block and survey checks escape the strict reader
findings.reproduction: Observe the return types of strict::read and strict::Pile::readings, then trace block() and survey() on a valid file.
findings.expected: File-backed operations that process secret payload should retain the strict contract past header parsing.
findings.observed: The returned ShardFile is the ordinary reader. block() and survey() compute CRC over the payload on the caller thread and do not enter the protected stack.
findings.impact: Reading a block or inspecting a file can process secret data outside the advertised boundary. The initial buffer remains protected.
findings.recommendedFix: Provide a strict reader with guarded lazy operations or validate/cache the required state inside the strict operation. Keep the lifetime/owner restriction explicit for any borrowed view.
findings.requiredVerification: Cover both reader entry points, repeated calls, absent stack admission and accepted ordinary file shapes.

findings.title: Reading a correction’s location also decodes the original and replacement symbols
findings.reproduction: Read the public position/kind through get or the iterator of a strict plan, without requesting its values.
findings.expected: Metadata access should read only metadata. Strict symbol access belongs in the protected callback.
findings.observed: get calls record and decodes both u16 fields. In local unoptimized Linux LLVM IR it reserves a 24-byte ordinary stack slot and passes it as the record return destination before projecting metadata.
findings.impact: An application can materialize recovery-word values in ordinary temporary storage merely by showing a position. This does not depend on the callback retaining a copy.
findings.recommendedFix: Have get decode only the position/kind offsets. Provide a strict plan view if ordinary symbol access is otherwise accidentally exposed.
findings.requiredVerification: Inspect a debug build for symbol loads on metadata-only access and cover get, iter and IntoIterator; verify the separate value accessor remains guarded.

findings.title: Strict recovery returns the computed digest in an ordinary printable error
findings.reproduction: Trace the existing digest-mismatch branch in rebuild and rebuild_into; inspect the type and formatting of the forwarded error.
findings.expected: A strict error should report failed integrity without copying a private intermediate into caller memory or diagnostics.
findings.observed: SetError::Digest carries both the stated hash and the actual hash of the reconstructed data. The latter differs from the public header; derived Debug prints all 32 bytes. The strict wrapper forwards that value from the protected-stack job.
findings.impact: A log or crash report can include a stable fingerprint of the reconstructed bytes. This matters especially for partially known or low-entropy material. No memory dump or leak was measured.
findings.recommendedFix: Map mismatches to a status-only strict error before returning from the protected closure. Keep detailed diagnostics confined to the portable API where appropriate.
findings.requiredVerification: Cover mismatches through both strict APIs; verify the error payload and Debug output contain no computed digest and output handling still follows the documented policy.

findings.title: The strict-mode example populates unchecked secret buffers
findings.reproduction: Follow the README’s strict-mode input and callback-destination construction under best-effort allocation.
findings.expected: The documented path for actual secrets should confirm required protection before storing any secret in caller-owned buffers.
findings.observed: The example fills Secret::with_capacity before checking its properties. The callback destination is also created with with_capacity and captured by the closure; strict::values checks the Changes buffer, not that destination.
findings.impact: The sample can put an input or recovered word into unlocked memory despite its comment describing protected output. The published example uses public constants; the risk is for applications following it with real input.
findings.recommendedFix: Show a checked helper that allocates, confirms lock/fork/dump properties for the supported platform, and only then accepts bytes. On Apple document the separate process-wide measure.
findings.requiredVerification: Exercise the documented path under a small lock budget and check that neither caller-supplied destination nor input is populated when its required protection is absent.

findings.title: for_data validates digest-specific size after it hashes the input
findings.reproduction: Trace for_data with DataDigest::Sha256 for a descriptor accepted without a digest and rejected with one.
findings.expected: The method documents that it rejects invalid facts before computing the digest.
findings.observed: The first new call passes None; Some(sha256(data)) is evaluated before the second constructor validates the digest-bearing shape.
findings.impact: The documented ordering is wrong for sizes beyond the digest bound; the metadata decoder itself rejects them correctly. No impractically large payload was tested.
findings.recommendedFix: Validate the digest-bearing layout with a placeholder before hashing, then set the computed digest in the validated facts.
findings.requiredVerification: Test ordering at the metadata boundary using a counting digest hook or a separate shape-validation helper without allocating a giant message.

remediation.evidence: strict.rs:183–249, buffer.rs:55–73 and strict.rs:45–73 gate caller buffers, new allocations and stack before use. Six strict Linux tests passed, including the non-skipped memory-limit child. Missing native evidence for this snapshot on the other supported systems. The checks here concern storage admission; operations that bypass admission appear below.
Sealed Held/HeldMut and the compile-fail test reject Vec. strict::read and Pile::readings return portable ShardFile handles; FileSet::without skips the strict gate (AUD-003-SEC001/002).

Public Change exposes only position and kind, Changes::values offers a callback and strict::values checks the list. get/iteration still decodes both payload words on the caller stack (AUD-003-SEC003). Deliberate copies made by a callback are outside the documented contract.

Strict main operations use a 512 KiB protected stack. Scaling tails are wiped; SHA state uses zeroize. Unguarded duplicate comparison, lazy CRC, metadata access and the mismatched digest still cross that boundary. See AUD-003-SEC001–004.

Both lockfiles use the registry archive at the same digest. All 19 upstream src/*.rs files, including subdirectories, matched the archive, unpacked build inputs and signed-tag source. The tag descends from the upstream native acceptance commit. Native upstream checks are historical.
TECHNICAL.md:256–258 distinguishes multiplication/CRC from the decoder, which branches on values. Source inspection, not a timing measurement.

Poll reserves for full membership before appending and reserves half the shard count for wrong holders; Finder bounds its locator list. Source and public multi-file vote regressions (src/file/set/vote.rs:250–258, src/correct.rs:494, tests/suite/votes.rs). Votes intentionally report locations.

Point and cyclic identities and ordered (index, length, bytes) enter SHA-256; apply verifies fingerprint and all records before any write. Tests change untouched symbols, order and code parameters (src/correct/plan.rs:139–203, src/cyclic/owned.rs:198, tests/suite/plans.rs:484, cyclic.rs:445).

Fallible metadata reservation and bounded extensions traced. On small alloc-only inputs, denial of each baseline allocation produced CodeError::Memory for encode (8), rebuild (7), redundancy (5), plan (10) and correct (7). The correct input was unchanged.

BySlot sorts without allocation; file output semantics distinguish refusals before writing from late failures after framing. In-place suite plus single-allocation refusal sweep for multi-file writing and repairs. src/file/set/sink.rs:99, src/file/writing.rs:90, tests/suite/in_place.rs:78,123.

Card-plan expected changes now use a fixed array. Other startup checks use infallible collect()/to_vec() (src/self_test.rs:271–273,290–295,364–366). The alloc-only test process ended with exit 134 on a 120-byte allocation. Replace the remaining fixed-size collections with arrays/fallible storage and compare borrowed slices. The regression must return passed()==false without terminating.
src/code.rs:62 and tests/suite/refusals.rs:253 distinguish the 256-byte scratch contract from the threshold; suite passed.
FileError::Memory and in-place docs detail early untouched versus late zeroed outputs. tests/suite/in_place.rs:78,123 and the allocator check exercise both output contracts.
src/file/facts.rs:85 rejects a digest-bearing size of 2^61 bytes; tests/suite/files.rs:267 validates the two descriptor boundary values. Separate early-hash issue in AUD-003-FUN001.
Two correction passes reuse the syndrome buffer and decoder room (src/cyclic/owned.rs:135–157,268). Ancillary metadata allocation is still possible; the old duplicated decoder workspace is gone.
The no-allocator self-test calls Header::file_into and compares all 86 bytes against a fixed answer (src/file.rs:139–157); the borrowed profile passed.

After validating inputs the common writer returns early on empty indexes. Its owned wrapper converts file_len to usize first (src/file/writing.rs:25,95). On 32-bit, threshold 1, 1 GiB input, one-byte blocks, a hypothetical file needs over 5 GiB. With zero requested files the owned method returns Memory; files_into returns success. Static geometry, no giant allocation. Move the empty return ahead of the conversion after validations.

The main platform paragraph now describes fallback and owner generation (TECHNICAL.md:265). Line 271 still says an ordinary Secret is refused at the lock limit; 273 treats Isolation::enter as a guarantee. Use checked constructors/confirmed measures, clarify cached child views and relay upstream's process-wide no-fork precondition while a protected stack runs (upstream src/stack.rs:63–67).

Digest enforcement at the high-level writer, one-member k=1 sets and the two file-format field identifiers are distinguished (src/file/facts.rs:72, src/file.rs:89, src/file/set.rs:127, TECHNICAL.md:381; digest/format suites).

Erased positions are tested before reading them in the cyclic search; documentation scopes this to source semantics and does not rule out speculative or widened loads. src/cyclic/words.rs:168,205; src/cyclic/decode.rs:122; TECHNICAL.md:205.

Two bytes control agrees_in scratch size on both sides of 256 and the accepted answer is checked against agrees (fuzz/fuzz_targets/calls.rs:49–54). Both 255/256 fixed smoke inputs returned success in the reviewer run; separate retained ASan fuzz evidence.
fuzz/examples/seeds.rs:16 creates the destination path; nightly seeds command wrote four files into a previously absent nested corpus.
Root and fuzz manifest/lock changes trigger audit.yml; two action steps name the right lockfiles. Both local advisory commands ran. Trigger wiring checked statically, no Actions run dispatched.
Cargo.toml requires alloc for the integration suite and example; CI selects all three profiles. The standard no-default command now passes with 29 unit tests on Linux. No new native CI run.

Erratum records both informational RustSec warnings, plus the distinct code/test commits 9c75fba and 92b842d. Historical logs and Git records were checked; current root scan also reports the two dev-dependency warnings.

README lists bytemuck under alloc, distinguishes self-test known answers and equivalent-entry-point checks, and lists the two profile counts (17/11); both self-test configurations passed at normal memory availability.
Both lockfiles and Cargo.toml resolve the immutable registry package; a Git force-push no longer controls these bytes.

limitations: Runtime acceptance is Linux x86-64 only. Windows, macOS and WASM were cross-checked. Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, ARM64 Linux and WASM were not executed in this audit. No GitHub run was dispatched for the working tree.
No new line-coverage measurement. The README value of 98.35% is historical. No claim was made about seeing a secret in swap, a core dump or an external process.
The long opt-in field proof was ignored in the ordinary profile tests. No independent five-target fuzz replay; the supplied post-pin logs are retained separately.

The callable lifecycle checks concern public synthetic data. The 32-bit empty-request case and extreme SHA limit were checked from code and representable geometry, without allocating giant messages. Unoptimized Linux IR was inspected at the affected metadata reader; this was not a multi-architecture assembly review.
The register uses snapshot SHA-256 in lieu of a fix or verification commit. The frozen brief excludes edits to the checkout; this Markdown/JSON pair, register and evidence are delivered outside it.
notes: The release pin is correct. The upstream 0.1.0 crate, source commit and both lockfiles agree; the earlier mutable-Git-reference finding AUD-001-BLD002 is verified.
The strong digest binding and stale-plan refusal now precede mutations for both RS code forms. A retained callback may intentionally copy returned data; the application is responsible for that copy.

The Apple policy waives per-page dump exclusion and does not require an Isolation report. A consumer requiring dump exclusion must confirm the appropriate process-level protection before handing over secrets. Strict payload calls refuse on Windows/WASM; metadata-only constructors may still succeed.

An ordinary fork between strict calls invalidates the assumption behind already parsed views. Pile stores borrowed slices, not fresh owners to recheck. Follow upstream’s no-fork rule while a protected stack is active and discard/reparse cached reader/set views in a child. This is a lifecycle limitation under the documented prohibition on using parent buffers in the child; it is not evidence of inherited secret data.

The currently inspected stego-core checkout uses reed-solomon-core from Git f6e2888 and secret-protection-core from Git fb2a6d3. No reed-solomon-core dependency was found in the inspected MnemoCode Rust manifests or lockfile. This audit establishes no consumer upgrade.
